reuse.why: Holidays are folded into getDateWithSkippedWeekend, but app.ts rebuilds 'd.isWeekend(date) || isHoliday(...)' inline because isWeekendOrHoliday is kept private, and the daily-skip rule gets no shared function.

duplication.why: The 'skipWeekend && frequency === daily -> drop weekend/holiday occurrences, else move them' logic is written three times (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange), and getDatesInRange also carries a redundant second holiday branch that its first branch already covers.

placement.why: Holiday and weekend checks live in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-vs-move policy is decided again in server/schedules/app.ts for each handler instead of in one shared weekend-rule function.

scope.why: Every edit serves the four steps; there are no unrelated changes.

maintainability.why: Weekend policy is split between a helper and three ad-hoc caller branches with magic over-fetch counts and a dead branch, and budget/schedule-template.ts still moves daily weekend occurrences and ignores holidays, so the paths already disagree.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange compose d.isWeekend || isHoliday themselves instead of a shared isWeekendOrHoliday or weekend-rule helper; budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList calls getDateWithSkippedWeekend without holidays or the daily skip.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily-skip branch appears as a filter closure in getNextDate, a filter-then-map with negated conditions in getUpcomingDates, and a map-to-null in getDatesInRange; the private isWeekendOrHoliday is re-spelled inline in app.ts.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter (its loop handles holidays cleanly). The daily-skip special case is re-implemented outside it in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, while schedule-template.ts bypasses both the holiday and the daily rules.
